headline: When motivation disappears—reconnecting to purpose and reigniting drive
universal_truth: Motivation isn't constant; it's rekindled through connection to meaning and small actions
fun_facts: Action often precedes motivation—starting small can spark larger engagement
Connecting to 'why' is more powerful than focusing on 'how'
Even 2 minutes of progress can restore a sense of momentum
discussion_questions: What originally drew you to learning?
What would achieving your goals feel like?
Who are you doing this for—including yourself?

hook.script: The fire went out. That spark that started you learning—you can't find it today. Motivation has vanished. You're here because you want it back. Let's find it together.

cliff.script: Should you wait for motivation to return or try to create it?

options.text: Action creates motivation more than motivation creates action—small steps generate momentum; waiting for feeling keeps you stuck; do something tiny to start the engine
options.response: Yes. The secret is: motivation follows action, not the other way around. Start with something ridiculously small. Two minutes. One page. One lesson. Momentum builds from motion.

options.text: Wait until you feel like it
options.response: That can work sometimes, but often feeling comes after doing. Try a tiny action first...

fact1.title: Remember Your Why
fact1.script: Why did you start this? What did you hope to become? Close your eyes and picture yourself having achieved your learning goals. How does that feel? That vision is your fuel.

fact2.title: The 2-Minute Rule
fact2.script: Promise yourself just 2 minutes. Anyone can do 2 minutes. Often, once you start, you continue. But even if you stop at 2 minutes, you've maintained your streak of action.

fact3.title: Phone a Friend
fact3.script: Tell someone about your goal. Accountability creates external motivation when internal drive fades. Sometimes we do for others what we won't do for ourselves.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Motivation is a fire that needs tending. When it dims, add small kindling—tiny actions, meaningful purpose, supportive people. The flame returns.

outro.script: Feeling any spark? Even a small one? Feed it. Do your 2 minutes. Then see what happens. The fire is still there—it just needs a little fuel.

growTrack.title: Motivation Rekindler - Find Your Spark
growTrack.learning_objective: Reconnect to purpose and take small action
growTrack.activity: Write down why you started learning. Picture your future self having achieved your goals. Now: do just 2 minutes of learning. Notice if momentum builds.
